paragraphs.bg: От понеделник до петък Петър е при баба Елена и дядо Георги в Пловдив. На масата в двора баба Елена слага ястие с боб и зеленчуци. „Бабо, къде е пицата?“, пита Петър. „Няма пица, Петре. Има боб, салата и маслини.“ Петър гледа маслините и не яде. „Тук е много скучно“, казва той. „Няма пица, няма приятели.“
paragraphs.nl: Van maandag tot en met vrijdag is Petar bij oma Elena en opa Georgi in Plovdiv. Op de tafel op het erf zet oma Elena een gerecht met bonen en groenten. ‘Oma, waar is de pizza?’ vraagt Petar. ‘Er is geen pizza, Petar. Er zijn bonen, salade en olijven.’ Petar kijkt naar de olijven en eet niet. ‘Het is hier heel saai,’ zegt hij. ‘Geen pizza, geen vrienden.’
paragraphs.en: From Monday to Friday Petar is with Grandma Elena and Grandpa Georgi in Plovdiv. On the table in the yard Grandma Elena puts a dish of beans and vegetables. ‘Grandma, where is the pizza?’ Petar asks. ‘There is no pizza, Petar. There are beans, salad and olives.’ Petar looks at the olives and doesn't eat. ‘It's very boring here,’ he says. ‘No pizza, no friends.’

paragraphs.bg: Във вторник дядо Георги казва: „Айде, Петре! Искам да ти покажа градината.“ Петър бавно върви след него. В градината има плодове и зеленчуци: домати, моркови, ябълки, круши. Петър опитва една круша. Хубава е, но това не е пица. „Виждаш ли онази диня зад крушите?“, пита дядо Георги. Петър спира. Това е най-голямата диня на света! Тя е по-голяма от него. „За петък е“, казва дядо Георги. „Тогава идва майка ти.“
paragraphs.nl: Op dinsdag zegt opa Georgi: ‘Kom op, Petar! Ik wil je de tuin laten zien.’ Petar loopt langzaam achter hem aan. In de tuin zijn fruit en groenten: tomaten, wortels, appels, peren. Petar proeft een peer. Die is lekker, maar dit is geen pizza. ‘Zie je die watermeloen daar achter de perenbomen?’ vraagt opa Georgi. Petar blijft staan. Dit is de grootste watermeloen ter wereld! Hij is groter dan Petar zelf. ‘Die is voor vrijdag,’ zegt opa Georgi. ‘Dan komt je moeder.’
paragraphs.en: On Tuesday Grandpa Georgi says, ‘Come on, Petar! I want to show you the garden.’ Petar walks slowly behind him. In the garden there are fruit and vegetables: tomatoes, carrots, apples, pears. Petar tries a pear. It's nice, but this isn't pizza. ‘Do you see that watermelon over there behind the pear trees?’ asks Grandpa Georgi. Petar stops. This is the biggest watermelon in the world! It is bigger than he is. ‘It's for Friday,’ says Grandpa Georgi. ‘Your mother is coming then.’

paragraphs.bg: В четвъртък дядо Георги и Петър трябва да донесат динята в кухнята. Двамата трудно я носят през двора. Петър вече не казва, че е скучно. Стигат до стълбата и бавно се качват. Тогава една котка минава между краката на дядо Георги. Динята пада от ръцете им, скача по стълбата и се счупва на две в краката на баба Елена. Сега по двора и по роклята ѝ има диня.
paragraphs.nl: Op donderdag moeten opa Georgi en Petar de watermeloen naar de keuken brengen. Met zijn tweeën dragen ze hem moeizaam over het erf. Petar zegt niet meer dat het saai is. Ze komen bij de trap en gaan langzaam omhoog. Dan loopt er een kat tussen de benen van opa Georgi door. De watermeloen valt uit hun handen, springt de trap af en breekt in tweeën aan de voeten van oma Elena. Nu zit er watermeloen op het erf en op haar jurk.
paragraphs.en: On Thursday Grandpa Georgi and Petar have to bring the watermelon to the kitchen. The two of them carry it across the yard with difficulty. Petar no longer says it is boring. They reach the stairs and slowly go up. Then a cat walks between Grandpa Georgi's legs. The watermelon falls from their hands, bounces down the stairs and breaks in two at Grandma Elena's feet. Now there is watermelon all over the yard and her dress.

paragraphs.bg: „Какво правите?“, пита баба Елена. Дядо Георги гледа динята. „Сега трябва да я изядем бързо“, казва той. Тримата седят на земята и ядат диня с ръце, без чинии и вилици. Лицето и тениската на Петър са мръсни. „Дядо, това е по-хубаво от пица!“
paragraphs.nl: ‘Wat doen jullie?’ vraagt oma Elena. Opa Georgi kijkt naar de watermeloen. ‘Nu moeten we hem snel opeten,’ zegt hij. Met zijn drieën zitten ze op de grond en eten watermeloen met hun handen, zonder borden en vorken. Het gezicht en het T-shirt van Petar zijn vies. ‘Opa, dit is lekkerder dan pizza!’
paragraphs.en: ‘What are you doing?’ asks Grandma Elena. Grandpa Georgi looks at the watermelon. ‘Now we have to eat it up quickly,’ he says. The three of them sit on the ground and eat watermelon with their hands, without plates or forks. Petar's face and T-shirt are dirty. ‘Grandpa, this is better than pizza!’

paragraphs.bg: В петък идва Мария. „Петре, в София те чака пица!“ „Пица ли? Мамо, пицата е скучно ястие.“ „Така ли?“, пита Мария. „Да. Може ли да живея тук?“ „Може“, казва баба Елена, „ако ядеш маслини.“ Петър дълго гледа маслините на масата. После бавно взема една.
paragraphs.nl: Op vrijdag komt Maria. ‘Petar, in Sofia wacht er pizza op je!’ ‘Pizza? Mama, pizza is een saai gerecht.’ ‘O ja?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Ja. Mag ik hier wonen?’ ‘Dat mag,’ zegt oma Elena, ‘als je olijven eet.’ Petar kijkt lang naar de olijven op tafel. Dan pakt hij er langzaam één.
paragraphs.en: On Friday Maria comes. ‘Petar, there's a pizza waiting for you in Sofia!’ ‘Pizza? Mum, pizza is a boring dish.’ ‘Really?’ asks Maria. ‘Yes. Can I live here?’ ‘You can,’ says Grandma Elena, ‘if you eat olives.’ Petar looks at the olives on the table for a long time. Then he slowly takes one.

paragraphs.bg: В събота Мария и Петър отиват до един магазин в центъра на града. Пътят минава през голяма градина. Слънцето е топло, но Мария е с широко яке. Портфейлът ѝ е в джоба на якето. Петър върви бавно и яде голям сандвич.
paragraphs.nl: Op zaterdag gaan Maria en Petar naar een winkel in het centrum van de stad. De weg loopt door een grote tuin. De zon is warm, maar Maria draagt een wijde jas. Haar portemonnee zit in de zak van de jas. Petar loopt langzaam en eet een groot broodje.
paragraphs.en: On Saturday Maria and Petar are going to a shop in the city centre. The road goes through a big garden. The sun is warm, but Maria is wearing a loose jacket. Her wallet is in the jacket pocket. Petar is walking slowly and eating a big sandwich.

paragraphs.bg: След малко едно дебело куче тича към тях. То скача върху Мария и дърпа якето ѝ със зъби. Един млад мъж бяга след кучето. „Извинете, госпожо! Той е добър, само много обича хората.“ „Всичко е наред“, казва Мария. Младият мъж дърпа кучето и го води към едно дърво. Мария и Петър продължават към магазина.
paragraphs.nl: Even later rent er een dikke hond op hen af. Hij springt tegen Maria op en trekt met zijn tanden aan haar jas. Een jonge man rent achter de hond aan. ‘Neemt u me niet kwalijk, mevrouw! Hij is lief, hij houdt alleen erg van mensen.’ ‘Alles is in orde,’ zegt Maria. De jonge man trekt de hond mee en brengt hem naar een boom. Maria en Petar lopen door naar de winkel.
paragraphs.en: A little later a fat dog runs towards them. It jumps up at Maria and pulls at her jacket with its teeth. A young man runs after the dog. ‘Excuse me, madam! He is good, he just loves people very much.’ ‘Everything is fine,’ says Maria. The young man pulls the dog and takes it towards a tree. Maria and Petar continue towards the shop.

paragraphs.bg: В магазина Мария взема хляб и хубав зехтин. „Колко струва този зехтин?“, пита тя. „Дванадесет“, казва госпожицата. Мария слага ръка в джоба си. Джобът е празен! И в чантата го няма. „Петре, портфейла ми го няма!“ Петър спира да яде. „Мамо, кучето! Якето ти! Може би портфейлът е на земята в градината?“ „Точно така!“, казва Мария. Тя обяснява на госпожицата. После тя и Петър бягат към градината.
paragraphs.nl: In de winkel pakt Maria brood en goede olijfolie. ‘Hoeveel kost deze olijfolie?’ vraagt ze. ‘Twaalf,’ zegt de jonge vrouw. Maria steekt haar hand in haar zak. De zak is leeg! Ook in haar tas zit hij niet. ‘Petar, mijn portemonnee is weg!’ Petar stopt met eten. ‘Mama, de hond! Je jas! Misschien ligt de portemonnee op de grond in de tuin?’ ‘Precies!’ zegt Maria. Ze legt het uit aan de jonge vrouw. Daarna rennen zij en Petar naar de tuin.
paragraphs.en: In the shop Maria takes bread and good olive oil. ‘How much does this olive oil cost?’ she asks. ‘Twelve,’ says the young woman. Maria puts her hand in her pocket. The pocket is empty! It isn't in her bag either. ‘Petar, my wallet is gone!’ Petar stops eating. ‘Mum, the dog! Your jacket! Maybe the wallet is on the ground in the garden?’ ‘Exactly!’ says Maria. She explains to the young woman. Then she and Petar run towards the garden.

paragraphs.bg: Те търсят по пътя и под дърветата, но портфейла го няма. След десет минути Мария вижда младия мъж в края на градината. Кучето лежи до него, а между краката му е портфейлът! Младият мъж дърпа портфейла, но кучето го държи със зъби. Мария също дърпа. Кучето мисли, че те играят, и дърпа още по-силно.
paragraphs.nl: Ze zoeken langs de weg en onder de bomen, maar de portemonnee is er niet. Na tien minuten ziet Maria de jonge man aan het eind van de tuin. De hond ligt naast hem en tussen zijn poten ligt de portemonnee! De jonge man trekt aan de portemonnee, maar de hond houdt hem met zijn tanden vast. Maria trekt ook. De hond denkt dat ze spelen en trekt nog harder.
paragraphs.en: They search along the road and under the trees, but the wallet isn't there. After ten minutes Maria sees the young man at the end of the garden. The dog is lying next to him, and between its legs is the wallet! The young man pulls at the wallet, but the dog holds it with its teeth. Maria pulls too. The dog thinks they are playing and pulls even harder.

paragraphs.bg: Тогава Петър показва сандвича си на кучето и го хвърля далече зад дървото. Кучето оставя портфейла и бяга след него. Сега то се интересува само от сандвича. Мария взема портфейла. Той е мръсен и грозен, но в него всичко е наред. „Браво, Петре! Вместо сандвич ти купувам сладолед.“ „Извинете, госпожо“, казва младият мъж. „Той само обича хората.“ „Да“, казва Мария и затваря чантата си. „Хората и портфейлите им.“
paragraphs.nl: Dan laat Petar zijn broodje aan de hond zien en gooit het ver achter de boom. De hond laat de portemonnee liggen en rent erachteraan. Nu is hij alleen nog in het broodje geïnteresseerd. Maria pakt de portemonnee. Hij is vies en lelijk, maar alles erin is in orde. ‘Goed zo, Petar! In plaats van een broodje koop ik een ijsje voor je.’ ‘Neemt u me niet kwalijk, mevrouw,’ zegt de jonge man. ‘Hij houdt alleen van mensen.’ ‘Ja,’ zegt Maria, en ze doet haar tas dicht. ‘Van mensen en van hun portemonnees.’
paragraphs.en: Then Petar shows his sandwich to the dog and throws it far behind the tree. The dog leaves the wallet and runs after it. Now it is only interested in the sandwich. Maria takes the wallet. It is dirty and ugly, but everything in it is fine. ‘Well done, Petar! Instead of a sandwich I'm buying you an ice cream.’ ‘Excuse me, madam,’ says the young man. ‘He just loves people.’ ‘Yes,’ says Maria, and she closes her bag. ‘People and their wallets.’

paragraphs.bg: В петък вечер Петър и Ана играят в двора. Господин Стоянов, старият им съсед, излиза по пижама и чехли. „Мици! Мици!“, вика той. Вече цял час търси котката си.
paragraphs.nl: Op vrijdagavond spelen Petar en Ana op de binnenplaats. Meneer Stojanov, hun oude buurman, komt naar buiten in pyjama en op pantoffels. ‘Mitsi! Mitsi!’ roept hij. Hij zoekt zijn kat al een heel uur.
paragraphs.en: On Friday evening Petar and Ana are playing in the yard. Mr Stoyanov, their old neighbour, comes out in pyjamas and slippers. ‘Mitsi! Mitsi!’ he calls. He has been looking for his cat for a whole hour.

paragraphs.bg: „Ето я!“, вика Петър. Котката е високо на голямото дърво в края на двора. Тя седи там и гледа към земята, но не слиза. Господин Стоянов иска да я стигне с чадъра си, но не може. „Аз съм стар, Петре. Не мога да се кача.“ „Аз мога!“, казва Петър. „Обещавам да ви помогна!“ „Ти?“, пита Ана. „Но ти се страхуваш от високо!“ „Не се страхувам“, отговаря Петър, но не гледа към дървото.
paragraphs.nl: ‘Daar is ze!’ roept Petar. De kat zit hoog in de grote boom aan het eind van de binnenplaats. Ze zit daar en kijkt naar de grond, maar ze komt niet naar beneden. Meneer Stojanov wil haar met zijn paraplu bereiken, maar dat lukt niet. ‘Ik ben oud, Petar. Ik kan niet naar boven.’ ‘Ik wel!’ zegt Petar. ‘Ik beloof dat ik u help!’ ‘Jij?’ vraagt Ana. ‘Maar jij bent bang voor hoogte!’ ‘Ik ben niet bang,’ antwoordt Petar, maar hij kijkt niet naar de boom.
paragraphs.en: ‘There she is!’ Petar shouts. The cat is high up in the big tree at the end of the yard. She is sitting there and looking at the ground, but she doesn't come down. Mr Stoyanov wants to reach her with his umbrella, but he can't. ‘I am old, Petar. I can't climb up.’ ‘I can!’ says Petar. ‘I promise to help you!’ ‘You?’ Ana asks. ‘But you are afraid of heights!’ ‘I'm not afraid,’ Petar answers, but he doesn't look at the tree.

paragraphs.bg: Господин Стоянов донася дълга стълба и я слага до дървото. Ана я държи, а Петър започва бавно да се качва. Минава една минута. Тогава Петър гледа към земята и спира. Земята е много далече! Краката му са слаби, а ръцете му държат стълбата много силно. „Петре, какво става?“, вика Ана. „Всичко е наред!“, вика Петър. Но той нито се качва, нито слиза.
paragraphs.nl: Meneer Stojanov brengt een lange ladder en zet die tegen de boom. Ana houdt hem vast en Petar begint langzaam te klimmen. Er gaat een minuut voorbij. Dan kijkt Petar naar de grond en stopt. De grond is heel ver weg! Zijn benen zijn slap en zijn handen houden de ladder heel stevig vast. ‘Petar, wat is er?’ roept Ana. ‘Alles is in orde!’ roept Petar. Maar hij gaat niet omhoog en niet omlaag.
paragraphs.en: Mr Stoyanov brings a long ladder and puts it against the tree. Ana holds it and Petar slowly starts to climb. One minute passes. Then Petar looks at the ground and stops. The ground is very far away! His legs are weak and his hands hold the ladder very tightly. ‘Petar, what's happening?’ Ana shouts. ‘Everything is fine!’ Petar shouts. But he goes neither up nor down.

paragraphs.bg: Котката го гледа. После тя става, минава бавно по дървото и скача върху рамото на Петър! Той вика. Котката скача на стълбата, после на земята. Сега тя седи до господин Стоянов и гледа Петър. „Петре, можеш да слезеш!“, вика Ана. Петър дълго не отговаря. После казва: „Ана, страхувам се.“
paragraphs.nl: De kat kijkt hem aan. Dan staat ze op, loopt langzaam door de boom en springt op Petars schouder! Hij schreeuwt. De kat springt op de ladder en daarna op de grond. Nu zit ze naast meneer Stojanov en kijkt naar Petar. ‘Petar, je kunt naar beneden komen!’ roept Ana. Petar geeft lang geen antwoord. Dan zegt hij: ‘Ana, ik ben bang.’
paragraphs.en: The cat looks at him. Then she gets up, walks slowly along the tree and jumps onto Petar's shoulder! He shouts. The cat jumps onto the ladder, then onto the ground. Now she is sitting next to Mr Stoyanov and looking at Petar. ‘Petar, you can come down!’ Ana shouts. For a long time Petar doesn't answer. Then he says: ‘Ana, I'm afraid.’

paragraphs.bg: След малко Иван пристига от болницата. Той вижда дървото, стълбата и сина си. Не пита, а се качва, взема Петър на ръце и слиза с него. Господин Стоянов държи Мици и дава на Петър голям шоколад. „Благодаря ти, Петре!“ „Но аз не помагам на котката“, казва Петър. „Цял час тя не слиза“, казва господин Стоянов. „Ти се качваш и тя скача. Значи ти ѝ помагаш!“ Петър яде шоколада и мисли. „Добре“, казва той. „Но следващия път вие се качвате.“
paragraphs.nl: Even later komt Ivan aan uit het ziekenhuis. Hij ziet de boom, de ladder en zijn zoon. Hij vraagt niets, maar klimt omhoog, neemt Petar op zijn armen en komt met hem naar beneden. Meneer Stojanov houdt Mitsi vast en geeft Petar een grote reep chocola. ‘Dank je, Petar!’ ‘Maar ik help de kat niet,’ zegt Petar. ‘Een heel uur komt ze niet naar beneden,’ zegt meneer Stojanov. ‘Jij klimt omhoog en ze springt. Dus je helpt haar!’ Petar eet de chocola en denkt na. ‘Goed,’ zegt hij. ‘Maar de volgende keer klimt u.’
paragraphs.en: A little later Ivan arrives from the hospital. He sees the tree, the ladder and his son. He doesn't ask, but climbs up, takes Petar in his arms and comes down with him. Mr Stoyanov holds Mitsi and gives Petar a big bar of chocolate. ‘Thank you, Petar!’ ‘But I'm not helping the cat,’ says Petar. ‘For a whole hour she doesn't come down,’ says Mr Stoyanov. ‘You climb up and she jumps. So you are helping her!’ Petar eats the chocolate and thinks. ‘All right,’ he says. ‘But next time you climb.’

paragraphs.bg: През октомври Яна има рожден ден. Тя става на единадесет години и кани Ана и още две момичета. Ана мисли цяла седмица какво да ѝ купи. Шоколад? Бонбони? Не, тениска с котка! Яна много обича котки.
paragraphs.nl: In oktober is Jana jarig. Ze wordt elf jaar en nodigt Ana en nog twee meisjes uit. Ana denkt een hele week na over wat ze voor haar zal kopen. Chocola? Snoep? Nee, een T-shirt met een kat! Jana houdt erg van katten.
paragraphs.en: In October it is Yana's birthday. She is turning eleven and invites Ana and two more girls. Ana thinks for a whole week about what to buy her. Chocolate? Sweets? No, a T-shirt with a cat! Yana loves cats very much.

paragraphs.bg: В събота Мария води Ана в един магазин в центъра. Там има много тениски, но само една е с котка. „Колко струва?“, пита Ана. „Дванадесет“, казва госпожицата. „Но този размер е за мъже.“ „Няма значение“, отговаря Ана. „Яна е висока. Тя е по-висока от мен.“ Мария гледа тениската. „Ана, не е ли много широка?“ „Не, мамо. Всичко е наред.“ Ана плаща и слага тениската в една малка чанта.
paragraphs.nl: Op zaterdag neemt Maria Ana mee naar een winkel in het centrum. Daar zijn veel T-shirts, maar er is er maar één met een kat. ‘Hoeveel kost het?’ vraagt Ana. ‘Twaalf,’ zegt de jonge vrouw. ‘Maar deze maat is voor mannen.’ ‘Dat maakt niet uit,’ antwoordt Ana. ‘Jana is lang. Ze is langer dan ik.’ Maria kijkt naar het T-shirt. ‘Ana, is het niet erg wijd?’ ‘Nee, mama. Alles is in orde.’ Ana betaalt en doet het T-shirt in een kleine tas.
paragraphs.en: On Saturday Maria takes Ana to a shop in the centre. There are many T-shirts there, but only one has a cat. ‘How much does it cost?’ Ana asks. ‘Twelve,’ says the young woman. ‘But this size is for men.’ ‘It doesn't matter,’ Ana answers. ‘Yana is tall. She is taller than me.’ Maria looks at the T-shirt. ‘Ana, isn't it very loose?’ ‘No, Mum. Everything is fine.’ Ana pays and puts the T-shirt in a small bag.

paragraphs.bg: В неделя Ана пристига при Яна. На масата има торта с ягоди, сладолед и студени напитки. Ана поздравява Яна за рождения ѝ ден и ѝ дава чантата. „Котка!“, вика Яна. „Много е хубава! Благодаря ти!“ Тя излиза от стаята и след една минута се връща с новата си тениска. Момичетата я гледат и не говорят. Тениската стига до коленете ѝ. Котката не е на гърдите ѝ, а на корема.
paragraphs.nl: Op zondag komt Ana bij Jana aan. Op tafel staan een taart met aardbeien, ijs en koude drankjes. Ana feliciteert Jana met haar verjaardag en geeft haar de tas. ‘Een kat!’ roept Jana. ‘Hij is heel mooi! Dank je!’ Ze gaat de kamer uit en komt na een minuut terug in haar nieuwe T-shirt. De meisjes kijken naar haar en zeggen niets. Het T-shirt komt tot aan haar knieën. De kat zit niet op haar borst, maar op haar buik.
paragraphs.en: On Sunday Ana arrives at Yana's. On the table there is a cake with strawberries, ice cream and cold drinks. Ana congratulates Yana on her birthday and gives her the bag. ‘A cat!’ Yana shouts. ‘It's very pretty! Thank you!’ She leaves the room and after one minute comes back in her new T-shirt. The girls look at her and don't speak. The T-shirt reaches her knees. The cat isn't on her chest, but on her belly.

paragraphs.bg: Ана гледа в пода. „Извинявай, Яно! Размерът е много голям. Можем да я сменим.“ Яна отива до огледалото и се гледа. Тя мисли малко. После ляга на дивана и затваря очи. „Няма значение“, казва тя. „Не искам да я сменям. Това е новата ми пижама!“ Двете момичета я гледат. Сега и те искат пижама с котка.
paragraphs.nl: Ana kijkt naar de vloer. ‘Sorry, Jana! De maat is erg groot. We kunnen het ruilen.’ Jana gaat naar de spiegel en bekijkt zichzelf. Ze denkt even na. Dan gaat ze op de bank liggen en doet haar ogen dicht. ‘Dat maakt niet uit,’ zegt ze. ‘Ik wil het niet ruilen. Dit is mijn nieuwe pyjama!’ De twee meisjes kijken naar haar. Nu willen zij ook een pyjama met een kat.
paragraphs.en: Ana looks at the floor. ‘Sorry, Yana! The size is very big. We can exchange it.’ Yana goes to the mirror and looks at herself. She thinks for a moment. Then she lies down on the sofa and closes her eyes. ‘It doesn't matter,’ she says. ‘I don't want to exchange it. These are my new pyjamas!’ The two girls look at her. Now they want pyjamas with a cat too.

paragraphs.bg: Вечерта Ана разказва на майка си за рождения ден. „Значи размерът е добър?“, пита Мария. „Точно така, мамо“, казва Ана. „За пижама.“
paragraphs.nl: 's Avonds vertelt Ana haar moeder over de verjaardag. ‘Dus de maat is goed?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Precies, mama,’ zegt Ana. ‘Voor een pyjama.’
paragraphs.en: In the evening Ana tells her mother about the birthday. ‘So the size is good?’ Maria asks. ‘Exactly, Mum,’ says Ana. ‘For pyjamas.’

paragraphs.bg: В събота Мария и Ана вървят по една улица в центъра на София. Пред един магазин ги спира висок мъж с малка книга в ръка. Той е турист. „Извинете! Колко е часът?“, пита той. Мария гледа часовника си. „Дванадесет и петнадесет.“ „Не разбирам“, казва туристът. Мария му показва часовника. Той го гледа и пак пита: „Колко е часът?“
paragraphs.nl: Op zaterdag lopen Maria en Ana door een straat in het centrum van Sofia. Voor een winkel houdt een lange man met een klein boekje in zijn hand hen staande. Hij is een toerist. ‘Pardon! Hoe laat is het?’ vraagt hij. Maria kijkt op haar horloge. ‘Twaalf uur vijftien.’ ‘Ik begrijp het niet,’ zegt de toerist. Maria laat hem het horloge zien. Hij kijkt ernaar en vraagt weer: ‘Hoe laat is het?’
paragraphs.en: On Saturday Maria and Ana are walking along a street in the centre of Sofia. In front of a shop a tall man with a small book in his hand stops them. He is a tourist. ‘Excuse me! What time is it?’ he asks. Maria looks at her watch. ‘Twelve fifteen.’ ‘I don't understand,’ says the tourist. Maria shows him the watch. He looks at it and asks again, ‘What time is it?’

paragraphs.bg: „Мамо, според мен той не иска да знае колко е часът“, казва Ана. Мъжът отваря книгата и дълго я гледа. „Искам да… искам да…“, казва той. После я затваря, слага ръка в джоба си и вика: „Няма! Няма!“ Мария смята, че той няма портфейл. Ана смята, че той иска да яде, и му дава сандвича си. Мъжът благодари, изяжда сандвича и пак вика: „Няма! Няма!“
paragraphs.nl: ‘Mama, volgens mij wil hij niet weten hoe laat het is,’ zegt Ana. De man slaat het boekje open en kijkt er lang in. ‘Ik wil… ik wil…’ zegt hij. Dan doet hij het dicht, steekt een hand in zijn zak en roept: ‘Is er niet! Is er niet!’ Maria denkt dat hij geen portemonnee heeft. Ana denkt dat hij wil eten en geeft hem haar broodje. De man bedankt, eet het broodje op en roept weer: ‘Is er niet! Is er niet!’
paragraphs.en: ‘Mum, I don't think he wants to know what time it is,’ says Ana. The man opens the book and looks at it for a long time. ‘I want to… I want to…’ he says. Then he closes it, puts a hand in his pocket and shouts, ‘There isn't! There isn't!’ Maria thinks he has no wallet. Ana thinks he wants to eat and gives him her sandwich. The man says thank you, eats the sandwich and shouts again, ‘There isn't! There isn't!’

paragraphs.bg: „Хотел ли търсите? Банка? Гара?“, пита Мария. „Не разбирам.“ Тогава мъжът прави с ръце малък прозорец около лицето си. „Лицето ви ли? Лекар ли търсите?“, пита Мария. „Съпругът ми е лекар.“ „Не разбирам!“
paragraphs.nl: ‘Zoekt u een hotel? Een bank? Het station?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Ik begrijp het niet.’ Dan maakt de man met zijn handen een klein raampje rond zijn gezicht. ‘Uw gezicht? Zoekt u een dokter?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Mijn man is dokter.’ ‘Ik begrijp het niet!’
paragraphs.en: ‘Are you looking for a hotel? A bank? The station?’ asks Maria. ‘I don't understand.’ Then the man makes a small window around his face with his hands. ‘Your face? Are you looking for a doctor?’ asks Maria. ‘My husband is a doctor.’ ‘I don't understand!’

paragraphs.bg: Ана гледа книгата в ръката му. „Интересно“, казва тя. „Може ли?“ Тя я взема и я отваря. От нея пада нещо малко. Ана го взема от земята и го отваря. Това е неговото лице! „Паспорт!“, вика мъжът. „Паспорт! Паспорт!“ „Значи търсите паспорта си, а той е при вас!“, казва Ана. „Не разбирам“, казва мъжът. „Благодаря! Благодаря!“
paragraphs.nl: Ana kijkt naar het boekje in zijn hand. ‘Interessant,’ zegt ze. ‘Mag ik?’ Ze pakt het en slaat het open. Er valt iets kleins uit. Ana raapt het op van de grond en doet het open. Dat is zijn gezicht! ‘Paspoort!’ roept de man. ‘Paspoort! Paspoort!’ ‘Dus u zoekt uw paspoort en u hebt het bij u!’ zegt Ana. ‘Ik begrijp het niet,’ zegt de man. ‘Dank u! Dank u!’
paragraphs.en: Ana looks at the book in his hand. ‘Interesting,’ she says. ‘May I?’ She takes it and opens it. Something small falls out of it. Ana picks it up from the ground and opens it. That's his face! ‘Passport!’ shouts the man. ‘Passport! Passport!’ ‘So you are looking for your passport, and you have it with you!’ says Ana. ‘I don't understand,’ says the man. ‘Thank you! Thank you!’

paragraphs.bg: Той пак слага паспорта в книгата. „Не там!“, вика Ана, но той вече гледа часовника на Мария. „Колко е часът?“, пита той. „Време е за кафе“, казва Мария и показва с ръка едно кафене на улицата. „Не разбирам“, казва туристът, но тръгва с тях.
paragraphs.nl: Hij stopt het paspoort weer in het boekje. ‘Niet daar!’ roept Ana, maar hij kijkt al op het horloge van Maria. ‘Hoe laat is het?’ vraagt hij. ‘Tijd voor koffie,’ zegt Maria, en ze wijst een café in de straat aan. ‘Ik begrijp het niet,’ zegt de toerist, maar hij gaat met hen mee.
paragraphs.en: He puts the passport back in the book. ‘Not there!’ shouts Ana, but he is already looking at Maria's watch. ‘What time is it?’ he asks. ‘Time for coffee,’ says Maria, and she points out a café in the street. ‘I don't understand,’ says the tourist, but he sets off with them.

paragraphs.bg: Дядо Георги е от едно малко село до Пловдив. През април там има голям празник. Дядо Георги кани цялото семейство. В събота Иван, Мария и децата пътуват до селото. Природата там е много красива: високи дървета, широко небе, чист въздух. Но Петър не гледа дърветата. „Искам да видя животните!“, казва той. Тича след едно пиле, а после едно куче тича след него.
paragraphs.nl: Opa Georgi komt uit een klein dorp bij Plovdiv. In april is daar een groot feest. Opa Georgi nodigt het hele gezin uit. Op zaterdag reizen Ivan, Maria en de kinderen naar het dorp. De natuur is daar erg mooi: hoge bomen, een wijde hemel, schone lucht. Maar Petar kijkt niet naar de bomen. ‘Ik wil de dieren zien!’ zegt hij. Hij rent achter een kip aan, en daarna rent er een hond achter hem aan.
paragraphs.en: Grandpa Georgi comes from a small village near Plovdiv. In April there is a big celebration there. Grandpa Georgi invites the whole family. On Saturday Ivan, Maria and the children travel to the village. The nature there is very beautiful: tall trees, a wide sky, clean air. But Petar isn't looking at the trees. ‘I want to see the animals!’ he says. He runs after a chicken, and then a dog runs after him.

paragraphs.bg: В центъра на селото има маси, вино и много хора. Те ядат, пият и играят хоро. Иван е с нов панталон и нов колан. Коланът е евтин, но красив. „Иване, сега ти водиш хорото!“, казва дядо Георги. „Аз ли? Но аз не знам как!“ „Лесно е. Хората се държат за коланите. Ти вървиш, а те вървят след теб.“
paragraphs.nl: In het centrum van het dorp zijn tafels, wijn en veel mensen. Ze eten, drinken en dansen de horo. Ivan draagt een nieuwe broek en een nieuwe riem. De riem is goedkoop, maar mooi. ‘Ivan, nu leid jij de horo!’ zegt opa Georgi. ‘Ik? Maar ik weet niet hoe!’ ‘Het is makkelijk. De mensen houden elkaar vast aan de riemen. Jij loopt en zij lopen achter jou aan.’
paragraphs.en: In the centre of the village there are tables, wine and a lot of people. They eat, drink and dance the horo. Ivan is wearing new trousers and a new belt. The belt is cheap but beautiful. ‘Ivan, now you lead the horo!’ says Grandpa Georgi. ‘Me? But I don't know how!’ ‘It's easy. People hold on to each other's belts. You walk, and they walk behind you.’

paragraphs.bg: Хорото започва. Иван е в началото, а до него е една стара жена от селото. Тя го държи за колана. Нейните ръце са много силни, а неговият колан е евтин. Иван върви по-бързо и по-бързо. В този момент коланът се скъсва. Панталонът започва да пада, но Иван не може да спре, защото цялото село върви след него. С едната ръка той води хорото, а с другата държи панталона си. „Тате, панталонът ти пада!“, вика Петър. Цялото село го чува.
paragraphs.nl: De horo begint. Ivan staat vooraan en naast hem staat een oude vrouw uit het dorp. Ze houdt hem vast aan zijn riem. Haar handen zijn erg sterk en zijn riem is goedkoop. Ivan loopt steeds sneller. Op dat moment breekt de riem. De broek begint af te zakken, maar Ivan kan niet stoppen, want het hele dorp loopt achter hem aan. Met de ene hand leidt hij de horo en met de andere houdt hij zijn broek vast. ‘Papa, je broek zakt af!’ roept Petar. Het hele dorp hoort het.
paragraphs.en: The horo begins. Ivan is at the front, and next to him is an old woman from the village. She holds him by the belt. Her hands are very strong, and his belt is cheap. Ivan walks faster and faster. At that moment the belt snaps. His trousers start to fall, but Ivan can't stop, because the whole village is walking behind him. With one hand he leads the horo and with the other he holds his trousers. ‘Dad, your trousers are falling down!’ shouts Petar. The whole village hears it.

paragraphs.bg: Мария тича до Иван, взема шала си и му го слага вместо колан. Сега той пак може да води с двете си ръце. Хората вървят след него до края. Един стар мъж го поздравява: „Браво! Хубав колан!“ „Неин е“, казва Иван и показва с ръка към Мария.
paragraphs.nl: Maria rent naar Ivan toe, pakt haar sjaal en doet die bij hem om in plaats van een riem. Nu kan hij weer met twee handen leiden. De mensen lopen tot het einde achter hem aan. Een oude man feliciteert hem: ‘Bravo! Mooie riem!’ ‘Die is van haar,’ zegt Ivan, en hij wijst naar Maria.
paragraphs.en: Maria runs up to Ivan, takes her scarf and puts it on him instead of a belt. Now he can lead with both hands again. The people walk behind him to the end. An old man congratulates him: ‘Well done! Nice belt!’ ‘It's hers,’ says Ivan, pointing at Maria.

paragraphs.bg: Вечерта семейството седи на една дълга маса с хората от селото. „Според мен това е най-хубавият празник от много години“, казва дядо Георги. „А ти, Петре, кое животно харесваш най-много?“ Петър гледа татко си и шала на Мария. „Татко“, казва той. Иван се смее най-силно.
paragraphs.nl: 's Avonds zit het gezin aan een lange tafel met de mensen uit het dorp. ‘Volgens mij is dit het mooiste feest in jaren,’ zegt opa Georgi. ‘En jij, Petar, welk dier vind jij het leukst?’ Petar kijkt naar zijn vader en naar de sjaal van Maria. ‘Papa,’ zegt hij. Ivan lacht het hardst.
paragraphs.en: In the evening the family sits at a long table with the people from the village. ‘I think this is the best celebration in many years,’ says Grandpa Georgi. ‘And you, Petar, which animal do you like best?’ Petar looks at his dad and at Maria's scarf. ‘Dad,’ he says. Ivan laughs the loudest.

paragraphs.bg: В петък Иван се връща от Берлин. Самолетът му пристига в седемнадесет часа. На летището има много хора и много багаж. Иван вижда куфара си, взема го и тръгва, защото децата го чакат. Пред сградата той намира такси. Младият мъж от таксито слага куфара в колата. „Толкова е тежък!“, казва той. „Какво носите, господине? Камъни ли?“ „Само дрехи и шоколад за децата“, отговаря Иван.
paragraphs.nl: Op vrijdag komt Ivan terug uit Berlijn. Zijn vliegtuig komt om zeventien uur aan. Op het vliegveld zijn veel mensen en is veel bagage. Ivan ziet zijn koffer, pakt hem en vertrekt, want de kinderen wachten op hem. Voor het gebouw vindt hij een taxi. De jonge man van de taxi zet de koffer in de auto. ‘Wat is die zwaar!’ zegt hij. ‘Wat neemt u mee, meneer? Stenen soms?’ ‘Alleen kleren en chocola voor de kinderen,’ antwoordt Ivan.
paragraphs.en: On Friday Ivan comes back from Berlin. His plane arrives at five p.m. There are a lot of people and a lot of luggage at the airport. Ivan sees his suitcase, takes it and sets off, because the children are waiting for him. In front of the building he finds a taxi. The young man from the taxi puts the suitcase in the car. ‘It’s so heavy!’ he says. ‘What are you carrying, sir? Stones?’ ‘Only clothes and chocolate for the children,’ Ivan answers.

paragraphs.bg: В апартамента Ана и Петър го чакат на вратата. „Татко, къде е шоколадът?“, пита Петър. Иван слага куфара в хола и го отваря. В него няма нито ризи, нито чорапи. Няма и шоколад. В него има само камъни, големи и малки, и малко пясък. Мария идва от кухнята и гледа куфара. „Иване, за камъни ли ходиш в Берлин?“ „Това не е куфарът ми!“, казва Иван. „Само е подобен на него!“
paragraphs.nl: In het appartement wachten Ana en Petar hem bij de deur op. ‘Papa, waar is de chocola?’ vraagt Petar. Ivan zet de koffer in de woonkamer en maakt hem open. Er zitten geen overhemden en sokken in. Er zit ook geen chocola in. Er zitten alleen stenen in, grote en kleine, en een beetje zand. Maria komt uit de keuken en kijkt naar de koffer. ‘Ivan, ga je voor stenen naar Berlijn?’ ‘Dit is mijn koffer niet!’ zegt Ivan. ‘Hij lijkt er alleen op!’
paragraphs.en: In the apartment Ana and Petar are waiting for him at the door. ‘Dad, where is the chocolate?’ Petar asks. Ivan puts the suitcase in the living room and opens it. There are no shirts or socks in it. There is no chocolate either. There are only stones in it, big and small, and a little sand. Maria comes from the kitchen and looks at the suitcase. ‘Ivan, do you go to Berlin for stones?’ ‘This isn’t my suitcase!’ says Ivan. ‘It only looks like it!’

paragraphs.bg: Ана търси в джоба на куфара и намира карта на София. На нея пише: Тодор Марков, хотел Рила. Иван се обажда в хотела. „Господин Марков? Предполагам, че вашият куфар е при мен.“ „Така ли?“, пита господин Марков. „А вашият е при мен! Толкова е лек! Много се притеснявам за камъните си. Идвам с такси!“
paragraphs.nl: Ana zoekt in het vak van de koffer en vindt een kaart van Sofia. Daarop staat: Todor Markov, hotel Rila. Ivan belt naar het hotel. ‘Meneer Markov? Ik neem aan dat uw koffer bij mij is.’ ‘O ja?’ vraagt meneer Markov. ‘En die van u is bij mij! Hij is zo licht! Ik maak me grote zorgen om mijn stenen. Ik kom met de taxi!’
paragraphs.en: Ana looks in the pocket of the suitcase and finds a map of Sofia. It says: Todor Markov, Hotel Rila. Ivan calls the hotel. ‘Mr Markov? I suppose your suitcase is with me.’ ‘Really?’ asks Mr Markov. ‘And yours is with me! It’s so light! I’m very worried about my stones. I’m coming by taxi!’

paragraphs.bg: След един час господин Марков е в хола, до двата куфара. Стар е и нисък, с дълга брада. Той отваря куфара си и гледа камъните. „Всичко е наред!“, казва той и се радва. „Защо носите камъни?“, пита Петър. „Търся ги по цял свят“, отговаря господин Марков. „Този е от морето, този е от планината. А този се ражда в огън.“ Той го дава на Петър: „За теб.“ После гледа Иван: „А шоколадът… Когато се притеснявам, хапвам нещо.“ Но Петър държи камъка в ръка и изобщо не мисли за шоколада.
paragraphs.nl: Na een uur is meneer Markov in de woonkamer, bij de twee koffers. Hij is oud en klein, met een lange baard. Hij maakt zijn koffer open en kijkt naar de stenen. ‘Alles is in orde!’ zegt hij, en hij is blij. ‘Waarom neemt u stenen mee?’ vraagt Petar. ‘Ik zoek ze over de hele wereld,’ antwoordt meneer Markov. ‘Deze komt uit de zee, deze uit de bergen. En deze wordt geboren in vuur.’ Hij geeft hem aan Petar: ‘Voor jou.’ Daarna kijkt hij naar Ivan: ‘En de chocola… Als ik me zorgen maak, neem ik een hapje.’ Maar Petar houdt de steen in zijn hand en denkt helemaal niet aan de chocola.
paragraphs.en: An hour later Mr Markov is in the living room, next to the two suitcases. He is old and short, with a long beard. He opens his suitcase and looks at the stones. ‘Everything is fine!’ he says, and he is glad. ‘Why do you carry stones?’ asks Petar. ‘I look for them all over the world,’ Mr Markov answers. ‘This one is from the sea, this one is from the mountains. And this one is born in fire.’ He gives it to Petar: ‘For you.’ Then he looks at Ivan: ‘And the chocolate… When I worry, I have a bite of something.’ But Petar holds the stone in his hand and doesn’t think about the chocolate at all.

paragraphs.bg: Следващата седмица Иван пак пътува. Той взема куфара си и спира. Защо е толкова тежък? Той го отваря. Върху ризите му има пет камъка от парка. Петър стои на вратата. „За господин Марков, татко!“, казва той.
paragraphs.nl: De week daarna reist Ivan weer. Hij pakt zijn koffer en stopt. Waarom is die zo zwaar? Hij maakt hem open. Op zijn overhemden liggen vijf stenen uit het park. Petar staat bij de deur. ‘Voor meneer Markov, papa!’ zegt hij.
paragraphs.en: The next week Ivan travels again. He takes his suitcase and stops. Why is it so heavy? He opens it. On top of his shirts there are five stones from the park. Petar is standing at the door. ‘For Mr Markov, Dad!’ he says.

paragraphs.bg: Неделя е. Иван, Мария и децата са за уикенда в планината. Цял уикенд пада сняг. Сега те стоят на спирката с багажа си и чакат автобуса за София. Той трябва да дойде по обед, в дванадесет. Вятърът е силен и студен, а Петър прави снежен човек.
paragraphs.nl: Het is zondag. Ivan, Maria en de kinderen zijn dit weekend in de bergen. Het hele weekend valt er sneeuw. Nu staan ze met hun bagage bij de halte en wachten ze op de bus naar Sofia. Die moet rond het middaguur komen, om twaalf uur. De wind is sterk en koud, en Petar maakt een sneeuwpop.
paragraphs.en: It’s Sunday. Ivan, Maria and the children are in the mountains for the weekend. Snow is falling all weekend. Now they are standing at the stop with their luggage, waiting for the bus to Sofia. It should come at noon, at twelve o’clock. The wind is strong and cold, and Petar is making a snowman.

paragraphs.bg: „Колко е часът?“, пита Мария. „Дванадесет и петнадесет“, казва Иван. Минават още петнадесет минути. Автобус няма. Иван се обажда за такси, но няма свободна кола. Никой не иска да кара в такъв сняг. „Дали автобусът изобщо идва?“, пита Мария. „Съмнявам се“, отговаря Иван.
paragraphs.nl: ‘Hoe laat is het?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Kwart over twaalf,’ zegt Ivan. Er gaan nog eens vijftien minuten voorbij. Er is geen bus. Ivan belt voor een taxi, maar er is geen auto vrij. Niemand wil in zulke sneeuw rijden. ‘Komt de bus eigenlijk wel?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Ik betwijfel het,’ antwoordt Ivan.
paragraphs.en: ‘What time is it?’ Maria asks. ‘A quarter past twelve,’ says Ivan. Another fifteen minutes go by. There is no bus. Ivan calls for a taxi, but there is no free car. Nobody wants to drive in snow like this. ‘Is the bus coming at all?’ Maria asks. ‘I doubt it,’ Ivan answers.

paragraphs.bg: Какво да правят сега? „Предлагам да се върнем в хотела“, казва Мария. „Там има огън в печката и топла супа.“ „Но в понеделник аз работя, а децата имат училище“, казва Иван. Ана показва една карта от хотела. „Ето! Гарата е след гората, до реката. В седемнадесет часа има влак за София.“ „Сигурна ли си?“, пита Мария. „Тук пише, мамо.“ „Аз предпочитам да играя в снега“, казва Петър. Багажът е тежък, а Петър е малък, и Мария се притеснява. Но автобус няма, а влак има. Тя се съгласява и те решават да вървят до гарата.
paragraphs.nl: Wat moeten ze nu doen? ‘Ik stel voor dat we teruggaan naar het hotel,’ zegt Maria. ‘Daar brandt een vuur in de kachel en is er warme soep.’ ‘Maar maandag werk ik, en de kinderen hebben school,’ zegt Ivan. Ana laat een kaart van het hotel zien. ‘Kijk! Het station ligt achter het bos, bij de rivier. Om zeventien uur gaat er een trein naar Sofia.’ ‘Weet je het zeker?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Het staat hier, mama.’ ‘Ik speel liever in de sneeuw,’ zegt Petar. De bagage is zwaar en Petar is klein, en Maria maakt zich zorgen. Maar er is geen bus en wel een trein. Ze stemt toe en ze besluiten naar het station te lopen.
paragraphs.en: What should they do now? ‘I suggest we go back to the hotel,’ says Maria. ‘There’s a fire in the stove there and warm soup.’ ‘But on Monday I work, and the children have school,’ says Ivan. Ana shows a map from the hotel. ‘Look! The station is past the forest, by the river. There’s a train to Sofia at five p.m.’ ‘Are you sure?’ Maria asks. ‘It says so here, Mum.’ ‘I prefer to play in the snow,’ says Petar. The luggage is heavy and Petar is small, and Maria worries. But there is no bus, and there is a train. She agrees, and they decide to walk to the station.

paragraphs.bg: Пътят през гората е тесен, а снегът стига до коленете на Петър. Иван носи Петър на ръце, Мария носи багажа, а Ана върви пред тях с картата. След два часа те виждат реката и малка сграда: гарата. В кафенето една жена им налива горещ чай. В седемнадесет часа те се качват на влака. Петър гледа през прозореца и вика: „Автобусът!“ На пътя до реката стои автобусът, а пред него лежи голямо дърво. Иван гледа Ана. „Браво! Картата ти е по-добра от автобуса!“
paragraphs.nl: De weg door het bos is smal en de sneeuw komt tot aan de knieën van Petar. Ivan draagt Petar in zijn armen, Maria draagt de bagage en Ana loopt met de kaart voor hen uit. Na twee uur zien ze de rivier en een klein gebouw: het station. In het café schenkt een vrouw hete thee voor hen in. Om zeventien uur stappen ze in de trein. Petar kijkt door het raam en roept: ‘De bus!’ Op de weg bij de rivier staat de bus, en ervoor ligt een grote boom. Ivan kijkt naar Ana. ‘Bravo! Jouw kaart is beter dan de bus!’
paragraphs.en: The road through the forest is narrow, and the snow reaches Petar’s knees. Ivan carries Petar in his arms, Maria carries the luggage and Ana walks ahead of them with the map. After two hours they see the river and a small building: the station. In the café a woman pours them hot tea. At five p.m. they get on the train. Petar looks through the window and shouts, ‘The bus!’ On the road by the river the bus is standing, and in front of it lies a big tree. Ivan looks at Ana. ‘Well done! Your map is better than the bus!’

paragraphs.bg: Вечерта те вече са в София. Децата вечерят в кухнята, когато Яна се обажда на Ана: „Знаеш ли? В понеделник няма училище заради снега!“ Петър тича в хола: „Мамо, татко, може ли пак да отидем в планината?“ Никой не му отговаря. Иван и Мария спят на дивана.
paragraphs.nl: ’s Avonds zijn ze al in Sofia. De kinderen eten in de keuken als Jana Ana belt: ‘Weet je wat? Maandag is er geen school vanwege de sneeuw!’ Petar rent naar de woonkamer: ‘Mama, papa, mogen we weer naar de bergen?’ Niemand antwoordt hem. Ivan en Maria slapen op de bank.
paragraphs.en: In the evening they are already in Sofia. The children are having dinner in the kitchen when Yana calls Ana: ‘Do you know what? On Monday there’s no school because of the snow!’ Petar runs to the living room: ‘Mum, Dad, can we go to the mountains again?’ Nobody answers him. Ivan and Maria are asleep on the sofa.

paragraphs.bg: В събота Петър има рожден ден и получава ново колело. То е леко и много бързо. Но в неделя има дъжд и силен вятър и той не може да излезе. В понеделник има слънце, но има и училище. Петър лежи в леглото, гледа през прозореца и мисли за парка. Тогава се сеща за нещо.
paragraphs.nl: Op zaterdag is Petar jarig en krijgt hij een nieuwe fiets. Die is licht en heel snel. Maar op zondag is er regen en harde wind en kan hij niet naar buiten. Op maandag is er zon, maar er is ook school. Petar ligt in bed, kijkt door het raam en denkt aan het park. Dan bedenkt hij iets.
paragraphs.en: On Saturday it’s Petar’s birthday and he gets a new bike. It’s light and very fast. But on Sunday there is rain and a strong wind and he can’t go out. On Monday there is sun, but there is also school. Petar lies in bed, looks through the window and thinks about the park. Then he thinks of something.

paragraphs.bg: „Мамо, не се чувствам добре“, казва той. „Имам болки в корема. Не мога да ходя на училище.“ Мария се притеснява и вика Иван. Иван е лекар от петнадесет години. Той влиза и слага ръка на главата на сина си. „Нямаш температура“, казва той. „Къде е болката? Може ли да видя?“ „Тук“, казва Петър и показва корема си. Иван слага ръка на корема му. Петър го гледа и нищо не казва. След една секунда се сеща и вика: „Мамо!“
paragraphs.nl: ‘Mama, ik voel me niet goed,’ zegt hij. ‘Ik heb pijn in mijn buik. Ik kan niet naar school.’ Maria maakt zich zorgen en roept Ivan. Ivan is al vijftien jaar dokter. Hij komt binnen en legt zijn hand op het hoofd van zijn zoon. ‘Je hebt geen koorts,’ zegt hij. ‘Waar zit de pijn? Mag ik het zien?’ ‘Hier,’ zegt Petar, en hij wijst zijn buik aan. Ivan legt zijn hand op zijn buik. Petar kijkt hem aan en zegt niets. Na een seconde schiet het hem te binnen en roept hij: ‘Mama!’
paragraphs.en: ‘Mum, I don’t feel well,’ he says. ‘I’ve got a pain in my tummy. I can’t go to school.’ Maria worries and calls Ivan. Ivan has been a doctor for fifteen years. He comes in and puts his hand on his son’s head. ‘You don’t have a fever,’ he says. ‘Where is the pain? May I see?’ ‘Here,’ says Petar, and he points to his tummy. Ivan puts his hand on his tummy. Petar looks at him and says nothing. After one second he remembers and shouts, ‘Mum!’

paragraphs.bg: Иван гледа сина си за момент. Той познава тази болест: тя идва в понеделник и минава в събота. „Тежка болест“, казва той на Мария. „Петър трябва да лежи цял ден. Без телевизор, без колело и без шоколад. За обяд: супа без сол. Ако не е по-добре, след обяд му правим инжекция.“ Петър лежи и се радва: няма училище!
paragraphs.nl: Ivan kijkt even naar zijn zoon. Hij kent deze ziekte: die komt op maandag en gaat op zaterdag over. ‘Een zware ziekte,’ zegt hij tegen Maria. ‘Petar moet de hele dag in bed liggen. Zonder televisie, zonder fiets en zonder chocola. Voor de lunch: soep zonder zout. Als het niet beter gaat, krijgt hij na de lunch een injectie.’ Petar ligt in bed en is blij: geen school!
paragraphs.en: Ivan looks at his son for a moment. He knows this illness: it comes on Monday and passes on Saturday. ‘A serious illness,’ he says to Maria. ‘Petar has to lie in bed all day. No television, no bike and no chocolate. For lunch: soup without salt. If he isn’t better, we’ll give him an injection after lunch.’ Petar lies in bed and is glad: no school!

paragraphs.bg: Но часовете минават бавно. През прозореца Петър вижда улицата и парка. Там някой кара велосипед. По обед Мария му носи супа. Тя е без сол и Петър я мрази.
paragraphs.nl: Maar de uren gaan langzaam voorbij. Door het raam ziet Petar de straat en het park. Daar fietst iemand. Rond het middaguur brengt Maria hem soep. Die is zonder zout en Petar haat die soep.
paragraphs.en: But the hours go by slowly. Through the window Petar sees the street and the park. Someone is riding a bicycle there. At noon Maria brings him soup. It has no salt and Petar hates it.

paragraphs.bg: След обяд Ана се връща от училище. „Какъв ден, Петре!“, казва тя. „Госпожата ти е на стадиона с децата. Играят, тичат и ядат сладолед!“ Петър става от леглото. „Татко, вече съм по-добре!“ „Съмнявам се“, казва Иван от вратата. „Такава болест не минава толкова бързо. Готов ли си за инжекцията?“ Петър гледа баща си. „Татко, лъжа те. Нищо ми няма.“ „Знам“, казва Иван. „Аз съм лекар.“
paragraphs.nl: Na de lunch komt Ana terug van school. ‘Wat een dag, Petar!’ zegt ze. ‘Je juf is met de kinderen in het stadion. Ze spelen, rennen en eten ijs!’ Petar komt uit bed. ‘Papa, het gaat al beter!’ ‘Dat betwijfel ik,’ zegt Ivan vanuit de deuropening. ‘Zo’n ziekte gaat niet zo snel over. Ben je klaar voor de injectie?’ Petar kijkt naar zijn vader. ‘Papa, ik lieg tegen je. Er is niets met me aan de hand.’ ‘Dat weet ik,’ zegt Ivan. ‘Ik ben dokter.’
paragraphs.en: After lunch Ana comes back from school. ‘What a day, Petar!’ she says. ‘Your teacher is at the stadium with the children. They’re playing, running and eating ice cream!’ Petar gets out of bed. ‘Dad, I’m already better!’ ‘I doubt it,’ says Ivan from the door. ‘An illness like that doesn’t pass so quickly. Are you ready for the injection?’ Petar looks at his father. ‘Dad, I’m lying to you. There’s nothing wrong with me.’ ‘I know,’ says Ivan. ‘I’m a doctor.’

paragraphs.bg: Следващия понеделник Петър е готов за училище още в седем часа. „Добре ли си?“, пита Мария. „Много добре, мамо! Изобщо нищо ми няма!“, вика Петър. „Можеш да питаш татко!“
paragraphs.nl: De volgende maandag is Petar al om zeven uur klaar voor school. ‘Gaat het?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Heel goed, mama! Er is helemaal niets met me aan de hand!’ roept Petar. ‘Je kunt het papa vragen!’
paragraphs.en: The following Monday Petar is ready for school as early as seven o’clock. ‘Are you all right?’ asks Maria. ‘Very well, Mum! There’s nothing wrong with me at all!’ shouts Petar. ‘You can ask Dad!’

title.nl: Oud en nieuw in de mist

paragraphs.bg: Вечерта срещу Нова година семейството иска да бъде на площада в центъра на София. В дванадесет часа там има фойерверки и Петър чака този момент от цял месец. „Разчитам на трамвая“, казва Иван. „Спирката е на нашата улица, а до площада са само петнадесет минути.“
paragraphs.nl: Op oudejaarsavond wil het gezin op het plein in het centrum van Sofia zijn. Om twaalf uur is daar vuurwerk, en Petar wacht al een hele maand op dit moment. ‘Ik reken op de tram,’ zegt Ivan. ‘De halte is in onze straat, en het is maar vijftien minuten naar het plein.’
paragraphs.en: On New Year’s Eve the family wants to be on the square in the centre of Sofia. At twelve o’clock there are fireworks there, and Petar has been waiting for this moment for a whole month. ‘I’m counting on the tram,’ says Ivan. ‘The stop is on our street, and it’s only fifteen minutes to the square.’

paragraphs.bg: В единадесет часа те излизат. Мъглата е толкова гъста, че не виждат другата страна на улицата, а по земята има лед. Те чакат на спирката. Минават десет минути, после петнадесет, но няма трамвай. „Къде е твоят трамвай?“, пита Мария. „Няма какво да чакате“, казва един мъж с куче. „Заради леда тази вечер няма трамваи.“
paragraphs.nl: Om elf uur gaan ze naar buiten. De mist is zo dik dat ze de overkant van de straat niet zien, en op de grond ligt ijs. Ze wachten bij de halte. Er gaan tien minuten voorbij, daarna vijftien, maar er komt geen tram. ‘Waar is jouw tram?’ vraagt Maria. ‘Wachten heeft geen zin,’ zegt een man met een hond. ‘Door het ijs rijden er vanavond geen trams.’
paragraphs.en: At eleven o’clock they go out. The fog is so thick that they can’t see the other side of the street, and there is ice on the ground. They wait at the stop. Ten minutes pass, then fifteen, but there is no tram. ‘Where is your tram?’ asks Maria. ‘There’s no point in waiting,’ says a man with a dog. ‘Because of the ice there are no trams tonight.’

paragraphs.bg: Иван гледа часовника си. „Трябва да тръгваме. До метрото са десет минути, ако вървим бързо.“ Но по леда никой не върви бързо. В мъглата те не виждат нито киното, нито църквата, а Петър пада два пъти. „Умирам от студ!“, вика той. „Още малко“, казва Мария. Тогава чуват някого в мъглата. „Извинете! Моля ви!“ Пред един вход на земята седи стара жена. „Не мога да стана“, казва тя.
paragraphs.nl: Ivan kijkt op zijn horloge. ‘We moeten gaan. Het is tien minuten naar de metro, als we snel lopen.’ Maar op het ijs loopt niemand snel. In de mist zien ze de bioscoop niet en de kerk ook niet, en Petar valt twee keer. ‘Ik sterf van de kou!’ roept hij. ‘Nog even,’ zegt Maria. Dan horen ze iemand in de mist. ‘Pardon! Alstublieft!’ Voor een ingang zit een oude vrouw op de grond. ‘Ik kan niet opstaan,’ zegt ze.
paragraphs.en: Ivan looks at his watch. ‘We have to go. It’s ten minutes to the metro if we walk fast.’ But nobody walks fast on the ice. In the fog they can see neither the cinema nor the church, and Petar falls twice. ‘I’m dying of cold!’ he shouts. ‘Just a little more,’ says Maria. Then they hear someone in the fog. ‘Excuse me! Please!’ In front of an entrance an old woman is sitting on the ground. ‘I can’t get up,’ she says.

paragraphs.bg: Иван е лекар и гледа коляното ѝ. „Не е толкова лошо“, казва той, „но не можете да вървите по леда.“ Той и Мария ѝ помагат да стане. В апартамента ѝ е топло. На масата има баница и само една чиния. „Вие трябва да тръгвате“, казва старата жена. „Децата искат да видят фойерверките.“ До дванадесет часа има само петнадесет минути, а площадът е далече. „Толкова голяма баница за една чиния?“, пита Петър. Старата жена не знае какво да каже. Мария отваря шкафа и слага на масата още една чиния, още една, още една и още една.
paragraphs.nl: Ivan is dokter en bekijkt haar knie. ‘Het valt mee,’ zegt hij, ‘maar u kunt niet over het ijs lopen.’ Hij en Maria helpen haar overeind. In haar appartement is het warm. Op tafel staan een banitsa en maar één bord. ‘U moet gaan,’ zegt de oude vrouw. ‘De kinderen willen het vuurwerk zien.’ Het is nog maar vijftien minuten tot twaalf uur, en het plein is ver. ‘Zo’n grote banitsa voor één bord?’ vraagt Petar. De oude vrouw weet niet wat ze moet zeggen. Maria doet de kast open en zet nog een bord op tafel, nog een, nog een en nog een.
paragraphs.en: Ivan is a doctor and looks at her knee. ‘It’s not that bad,’ he says, ‘but you can’t walk on the ice.’ He and Maria help her get up. It is warm in her apartment. On the table there is a banitsa and only one plate. ‘You have to go,’ says the old woman. ‘The children want to see the fireworks.’ There are only fifteen minutes until twelve o’clock, and the square is far away. ‘Such a big banitsa for one plate?’ asks Petar. The old woman doesn’t know what to say. Maria opens the cupboard and puts another plate on the table, another, another and another.

paragraphs.bg: По телевизора показват площада. Хората там гледат небето, но виждат само мъгла. Петър вика с тях: „Пет! Четири! Три! Две! Едно!“ „Честита Нова година!“, казва Иван. Старата жена реже баницата. В нея има късмети. На късмета на Петър пише: Пътуване. „До площада ли?“, пита Иван. Старата жена дълго гледа своя късмет. После го показва на Мария. На него пише: Нови приятели.
paragraphs.nl: Op de televisie laten ze het plein zien. De mensen daar kijken naar de lucht, maar ze zien alleen mist. Petar roept met hen mee: ‘Vijf! Vier! Drie! Twee! Eén!’ ‘Gelukkig nieuwjaar!’ zegt Ivan. De oude vrouw snijdt de banitsa. Er zitten geluksbriefjes in. Op dat van Petar staat: Een reis. ‘Naar het plein?’ vraagt Ivan. De oude vrouw kijkt lang naar haar eigen briefje. Daarna laat ze het aan Maria zien. Daarop staat: Nieuwe vrienden.
paragraphs.en: On television they show the square. The people there are looking at the sky, but they see only fog. Petar shouts along with them: ‘Five! Four! Three! Two! One!’ ‘Happy New Year!’ says Ivan. The old woman cuts the banitsa. There are lucky notes in it. Petar’s says: A journey. ‘To the square?’ asks Ivan. The old woman looks at her own note for a long time. Then she shows it to Maria. It says: New friends.

paragraphs.bg: Една събота през септември Иван и Петър отиват на пазара за домати и хляб. Петър има и свои пари от баба Елена. Той спира пред една жена с кокошки. „Колко струва тази?“, пита той. „Пет евро“, казва жената. „Петре, ние купуваме яйцата от супермаркета“, казва Иван. „Но парите са мои!“ „Добре. Твоите пари, твоята кокошка. Значи ти я носиш в трамвая.“
paragraphs.nl: Op een zaterdag in september gaan Ivan en Petar naar de markt voor tomaten en brood. Petar heeft ook zijn eigen geld, van oma Elena. Hij blijft staan bij een vrouw met kippen. ‘Hoeveel kost deze?’ vraagt hij. ‘Vijf euro,’ zegt de vrouw. ‘Petar, wij kopen onze eieren in de supermarkt,’ zegt Ivan. ‘Maar het geld is van mij!’ ‘Goed. Jouw geld, jouw kip. Dus jij draagt haar in de tram.’
paragraphs.en: One Saturday in September Ivan and Petar go to the market for tomatoes and bread. Petar also has his own money, from Grandma Elena. He stops in front of a woman with hens. ‘How much is this one?’ he asks. ‘Five euros,’ says the woman. ‘Petar, we buy our eggs at the supermarket,’ says Ivan. ‘But the money is mine!’ ‘All right. Your money, your hen. So you carry her on the tram.’

paragraphs.bg: Трамваят е пълен. Каква горещина! Петър седи с чантата в ръце. В нея е кокошката. „Момче, какво имаш в тази чанта?“, пита една жена. „Нищо“, казва Петър. Чантата започва да вика. „Нищо ли?“, пита жената. Трамваят спира пред библиотеката, вратите се отварят и кокошката скача от чантата.
paragraphs.nl: De tram zit vol. Wat een hitte! Petar zit met de tas in zijn handen. Daarin zit de kip. ‘Jongen, wat heb je in die tas?’ vraagt een vrouw. ‘Niets,’ zegt Petar. De tas begint te schreeuwen. ‘Niets?’ vraagt de vrouw. De tram stopt voor de bibliotheek, de deuren gaan open en de kip springt uit de tas.
paragraphs.en: The tram is full. What heat! Petar is sitting with the bag in his hands. The hen is in it. ‘Boy, what do you have in that bag?’ asks a woman. ‘Nothing,’ says Petar. The bag starts to shout. ‘Nothing?’ asks the woman. The tram stops in front of the library, the doors open and the hen jumps out of the bag.

paragraphs.bg: Петър и Иван слизат след нея, но тя вече е в двора на една църква. Там има цветя и тя спира да хапне. Петър иска да я хване, но не успява. Иван тича след тях с доматите и хляба. Пред музея един мъж с карта в ръка го спира. „Говорите ли английски?“ „Не сега!“, вика Иван. Кокошката вече е в музея.
paragraphs.nl: Petar en Ivan stappen achter haar uit, maar ze is al op de binnenplaats van een kerk. Daar staan bloemen, en ze stopt voor een hapje. Petar wil haar pakken, maar het lukt hem niet. Ivan rent hen achterna met de tomaten en het brood. Voor het museum houdt een man met een kaart in zijn hand hem tegen. ‘Spreekt u Engels?’ ‘Nu niet!’ roept Ivan. De kip is al in het museum.
paragraphs.en: Petar and Ivan get off after her, but she is already in the yard of a church. There are flowers there, and she stops for a bite. Petar wants to catch her, but he doesn’t manage. Ivan runs after them with the tomatoes and the bread. In front of the museum a man with a map in his hand stops him. ‘Do you speak English?’ ‘Not now!’ shouts Ivan. The hen is already in the museum.

paragraphs.bg: В голямата стая тя стои до една птица от камък. Тогава Петър си спомня какво прави дядо Георги с кокошките си. Момчето взема малко хляб от баща си, слага го на пода и чака. Кокошката идва и започва да яде. Петър я хваща с две ръце. „Браво!“, казва жената на входа. „А сега три билета, моля.“ „Три ли?“, пита Иван. „Ами кокошката не е ли в музея?“, казва тя.
paragraphs.nl: In de grote zaal staat ze naast een vogel van steen. Dan herinnert Petar zich wat opa Georgi met zijn kippen doet. De jongen neemt een beetje brood van zijn vader, legt het op de vloer en wacht. De kip komt en begint te eten. Petar pakt haar met twee handen. ‘Bravo!’ zegt de vrouw bij de ingang. ‘En nu drie kaartjes, alstublieft.’ ‘Drie?’ vraagt Ivan. ‘Maar de kip is toch ook in het museum?’ zegt ze.
paragraphs.en: In the big room she is standing next to a bird of stone. Then Petar remembers what Grandpa Georgi does with his hens. The boy takes a little bread from his father, puts it on the floor and waits. The hen comes and starts to eat. Petar catches her with both hands. ‘Bravo!’ says the woman at the entrance. ‘And now three tickets, please.’ ‘Three?’ asks Ivan. ‘Well, isn’t the hen in the museum?’ she says.

paragraphs.bg: Вечерта Мария стои на вратата на хола. На дивана седи кокошка. „Иване, какво е това?“ „Кокошката на Петър“, казва Иван. „Тя вече познава града по-добре от теб.“ „Понякога не знам кой от двама ви е детето“, казва Мария.
paragraphs.nl: ’s Avonds staat Maria in de deur van de woonkamer. Op de bank zit een kip. ‘Ivan, wat is dit?’ ‘De kip van Petar,’ zegt Ivan. ‘Ze kent de stad al beter dan jij.’ ‘Soms weet ik niet wie van jullie tweeën het kind is,’ zegt Maria.
paragraphs.en: In the evening Maria stands in the door of the living room. On the sofa sits a hen. ‘Ivan, what is this?’ ‘Petar’s hen,’ says Ivan. ‘She already knows the city better than you do.’ ‘Sometimes I don’t know which of you two is the child,’ says Maria.

paragraphs.bg: На следващия ден на дивана има яйце. Мария го вари и Петър закусва с него. Иван си мисли: пет евро за кокошката, три билета за музея, цяла събота по улиците. „Това е най-скъпото яйце в София“, казва той. „Скъпо е, но е мое“, казва Петър с пълна уста.
paragraphs.nl: De volgende dag ligt er een ei op de bank. Maria kookt het en Petar eet het bij het ontbijt. Ivan denkt: vijf euro voor de kip, drie kaartjes voor het museum, een hele zaterdag op straat. ‘Dit is het duurste ei van Sofia,’ zegt hij. ‘Het is duur, maar het is van mij,’ zegt Petar met zijn mond vol.
paragraphs.en: The next day there is an egg on the sofa. Maria boils it and Petar has it for breakfast. Ivan thinks: five euros for the hen, three tickets for the museum, a whole Saturday on the streets. ‘This is the most expensive egg in Sofia,’ he says. ‘It’s expensive, but it’s mine,’ says Petar with his mouth full.

paragraphs.bg: Коледа е и пада сняг. Ана и Петър гледат през прозореца. На улицата господин Стоянов, старият им съсед, върви бавно с малка чанта. Семейството му живее далече, в друга държава, и той винаги е сам на Коледа. „Това не е хубаво“, казва Ана. „Предлагам да му направим торта!“
paragraphs.nl: Het is Kerstmis en er valt sneeuw. Ana en Petar kijken uit het raam. Op straat loopt meneer Stojanov, hun oude buurman, langzaam met een kleine tas. Zijn familie woont ver weg, in een ander land, en met Kerstmis is hij altijd alleen. ‘Dat is niet leuk,’ zegt Ana. ‘Ik stel voor dat we een taart voor hem maken!’
paragraphs.en: It’s Christmas and snow is falling. Ana and Petar are looking out of the window. In the street Mr Stoyanov, their old neighbour, is walking slowly with a small bag. His family lives far away, in another country, and he is always alone at Christmas. ‘That isn’t nice,’ says Ana. ‘I suggest we make him a cake!’

paragraphs.bg: Мария е заета с вечерята и им дава рецепта от баба Елена. „Можете да се справите“, казва тя. Ана чете рецептата: шест яйца, масло, мляко, две чаши захар и малко сол. На рафта има две малки кутии, подобни една на друга. Петър взема едната. „Това ли е захарта?“, пита той. „Да, да“, казва Ана, но тя гледа рецептата, а не кутията. Петър слага две чаши в голямата купа, а после и малко от другата кутия.
paragraphs.nl: Maria heeft het druk met het avondeten en geeft hun een recept van oma Elena. ‘Jullie kunnen het wel,’ zegt ze. Ana leest het recept: zes eieren, boter, melk, twee kopjes suiker en een beetje zout. Op de plank staan twee kleine dozen die op elkaar lijken. Petar pakt er een. ‘Is dit de suiker?’ vraagt hij. ‘Ja, ja,’ zegt Ana, maar ze kijkt naar het recept en niet naar de doos. Petar doet twee kopjes in de grote kom, en daarna ook een beetje uit de andere doos.
paragraphs.en: Maria is busy with dinner and gives them a recipe from Grandma Elena. ‘You can manage,’ she says. Ana reads the recipe: six eggs, butter, milk, two cups of sugar and a little salt. On the shelf there are two small boxes that look alike. Petar takes one. ‘Is this the sugar?’ he asks. ‘Yes, yes,’ says Ana, but she is looking at the recipe, not at the box. Petar puts two cups in the big bowl, and then a little from the other box too.

paragraphs.bg: Следобед тортата се пече във фурната. Когато е готова, тя е висока и красива. Петър взема нож. „Може ли да опитам?“ „Не!“, казва Ана. „Цялата торта е за господин Стоянов!“ Тя я слага в голяма кутия и двамата се качват на следващия етаж.
paragraphs.nl: ’s Middags bakt de taart in de oven. Als hij klaar is, is hij hoog en mooi. Petar pakt een mes. ‘Mag ik proeven?’ ‘Nee!’ zegt Ana. ‘De hele taart is voor meneer Stojanov!’ Ze doet hem in een grote doos en met z’n tweeën gaan ze naar de volgende verdieping.
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon the cake bakes in the oven. When it is ready, it is tall and beautiful. Petar picks up a knife. ‘Can I taste it?’ ‘No!’ says Ana. ‘The whole cake is for Mr Stoyanov!’ She puts it in a big box and the two of them go up to the next floor.

paragraphs.bg: Господин Стоянов не очаква гости. Той отваря вратата по пижама и чехли. „Честита Коледа!“, викат децата. Той гледа кутията и дълго не казва нищо. „От много години никой не ми прави торта“, казва той. „Заповядайте!“
paragraphs.nl: Meneer Stojanov verwacht geen gasten. Hij doet de deur open in pyjama en op pantoffels. ‘Vrolijk kerstfeest!’ roepen de kinderen. Hij kijkt naar de doos en zegt lange tijd niets. ‘Al heel veel jaren maakt niemand een taart voor mij,’ zegt hij. ‘Kom binnen!’
paragraphs.en: Mr Stoyanov isn’t expecting guests. He opens the door in pyjamas and slippers. ‘Merry Christmas!’ the children shout. He looks at the box and says nothing for a long time. ‘Nobody has made me a cake for many years,’ he says. ‘Come in!’

paragraphs.bg: В кухнята той реже голямо парче и хапва. После спира. Очите му стават големи. Той си налива чаша вода и я пие бавно. „Хубава ли е?“, пита Ана. „Това не е обикновена торта“, казва той. „Много е специална.“ „Може ли и аз?“, пита Петър. Той хапва и отваря широко уста. „Ана, това е сол!“ Ана опитва. „Кутиите! Извинете, господин Стоянов! Две чаши сол!“
paragraphs.nl: In de keuken snijdt hij een groot stuk af en neemt een hap. Dan stopt hij. Zijn ogen worden groot. Hij schenkt een glas water in en drinkt het langzaam op. ‘Is hij lekker?’ vraagt Ana. ‘Dit is geen gewone taart,’ zegt hij. ‘Hij is heel bijzonder.’ ‘Mag ik ook?’ vraagt Petar. Hij neemt een hap en doet zijn mond wijd open. ‘Ana, dit is zout!’ Ana proeft. ‘De dozen! Neemt u me niet kwalijk, meneer Stojanov! Twee kopjes zout!’
paragraphs.en: In the kitchen he cuts a big piece and takes a bite. Then he stops. His eyes grow big. He pours himself a glass of water and drinks it slowly. ‘Is it good?’ asks Ana. ‘This is no ordinary cake,’ he says. ‘It’s very special.’ ‘Can I have some too?’ asks Petar. He takes a bite and opens his mouth wide. ‘Ana, this is salt!’ Ana tastes it. ‘The boxes! Excuse me, Mr Stoyanov! Two cups of salt!’

paragraphs.bg: Господин Стоянов се смее толкова силно, че очилата му падат. „Баща ви е моят лекар“, казва той, „и винаги ми казва: никаква захар! Най-после има торта за мен!“ Вечерта той не е сам. Мария и Иван го канят на вечеря и той идва с кутията. След вечерята Мария пита: „Искате ли торта?“ „Благодаря, имам си“, казва той, отваря кутията и реже едно парче. „Какво ядете, господин Стоянов?“, пита Иван. „Никаква захар, Иване!“
paragraphs.nl: Meneer Stojanov lacht zo hard dat zijn bril valt. ‘Jullie vader is mijn dokter,’ zegt hij, ‘en hij zegt altijd tegen me: helemaal geen suiker! Eindelijk is er een taart voor mij!’ ’s Avonds is hij niet alleen. Maria en Ivan nodigen hem uit voor het avondeten en hij komt met de doos. Na het eten vraagt Maria: ‘Wilt u taart?’ ‘Dank u, ik heb mijn eigen taart,’ zegt hij, en hij maakt de doos open en snijdt een stuk af. ‘Wat eet u daar, meneer Stojanov?’ vraagt Ivan. ‘Helemaal geen suiker, Ivan!’
paragraphs.en: Mr Stoyanov laughs so hard that his glasses fall off. ‘Your father is my doctor,’ he says, ‘and he always tells me: no sugar at all! At last there is a cake for me!’ In the evening he isn’t alone. Maria and Ivan invite him to dinner and he comes with the box. After dinner Maria asks, ‘Would you like some cake?’ ‘Thank you, I have my own,’ he says, opens the box and cuts a piece. ‘What are you eating, Mr Stoyanov?’ asks Ivan. ‘No sugar at all, Ivan!’

paragraphs.bg: Иван е зает човек и често работи до вечерта. Мария много обича театъра, но от две години не ходи там. Затова той решава да купи два билета. Купува ги бързо, между двама пациенти, слага ги в джоба си и не казва нищо на Мария.
paragraphs.nl: Ivan is een drukbezet man en werkt vaak tot de avond. Maria houdt erg van het theater, maar ze gaat er al twee jaar niet heen. Daarom besluit hij twee kaartjes te kopen. Hij koopt ze snel, tussen twee patiënten door, stopt ze in zijn zak en zegt niets tegen Maria.
paragraphs.en: Ivan is a busy man and often works until the evening. Maria loves the theatre very much, but she hasn’t been there for two years. So he decides to buy two tickets. He buys them quickly, between two patients, puts them in his pocket and says nothing to Maria.

paragraphs.bg: В събота следобед той ѝ показва билетите. „Тази вечер отиваме на театър!“ Мария се радва. Тя е с дълга рокля и тънки обувки, а Иван е с костюм. Тя взема само леко палто, защото с такси не е далече.
paragraphs.nl: Op zaterdagmiddag laat hij haar de kaartjes zien. ‘Vanavond gaan we naar het theater!’ Maria is blij. Ze draagt een lange jurk en dunne schoenen, en Ivan een pak. Ze neemt alleen een lichte jas mee, want met de taxi is het niet ver.
paragraphs.en: On Saturday afternoon he shows her the tickets. ‘Tonight we’re going to the theatre!’ Maria is glad. She is wearing a long dress and thin shoes, and Ivan a suit. She only takes a light coat, because by taxi it isn’t far.

paragraphs.bg: В седем часа те са пред театъра. На входа една жена гледа билетите на хората. Иван ѝ дава двата билета. Тя ги гледа дълго. „Извинете, господине, но датата на билетите ви е друга.“ „Какво означава това?“, пита Иван. „Те са за тринадесети април. А сега е ноември.“ Иван гледа датата. Тринадесети април! „Невъзможно!“, казва той. „Може ли да купя други?“ „За тази вечер няма нито едно свободно място.“
paragraphs.nl: Om zeven uur staan ze voor het theater. Bij de ingang bekijkt een vrouw de kaartjes van de mensen. Ivan geeft haar de twee kaartjes. Ze kijkt er lang naar. ‘Neemt u me niet kwalijk, meneer, maar op uw kaartjes staat een andere datum.’ ‘Wat betekent dat?’ vraagt Ivan. ‘Ze zijn voor dertien april. En het is nu november.’ Ivan kijkt naar de datum. Dertien april! ‘Onmogelijk!’ zegt hij. ‘Kan ik andere kopen?’ ‘Voor vanavond is er geen enkele plaats vrij.’
paragraphs.en: At seven o’clock they are in front of the theatre. At the entrance a woman is looking at people’s tickets. Ivan gives her the two tickets. She looks at them for a long time. ‘Excuse me, sir, but the date on your tickets is a different one.’ ‘What does that mean?’ asks Ivan. ‘They are for the thirteenth of April. And now it’s November.’ Ivan looks at the date. The thirteenth of April! ‘Impossible!’ he says. ‘Can I buy others?’ ‘There isn’t a single free seat for tonight.’

paragraphs.bg: Те излизат на улицата. Какъв студ! Има само два градуса, вятърът е силен, а Мария е с тънките си обувки. Иван не знае какво да каже. „Извинявай“, казва той. „Искам само да имаш една специална вечер.“ Мария го гледа за момент. После започва да се смее. „Иване! Само ти можеш да ме заведеш на театър през ноември с билети за април!“ „Какво да правим сега?“, пита той. „Децата са при съседа, а аз съм с най-хубавата си рокля. Тази вечер е наша!“
paragraphs.nl: Ze gaan naar buiten, de straat op. Wat een kou! Het is maar twee graden, de wind is sterk en Maria heeft haar dunne schoenen aan. Ivan weet niet wat hij moet zeggen. ‘Sorry,’ zegt hij. ‘Ik wil alleen dat je een bijzondere avond hebt.’ Maria kijkt hem even aan. Dan begint ze te lachen. ‘Ivan! Alleen jij kunt me in november meenemen naar het theater met kaartjes voor april!’ ‘Wat moeten we nu doen?’ vraagt hij. ‘De kinderen zijn bij de buurman en ik heb mijn mooiste jurk aan. Deze avond is van ons!’
paragraphs.en: They go out into the street. How cold it is! It’s only two degrees, the wind is strong, and Maria is in her thin shoes. Ivan doesn’t know what to say. ‘I’m sorry,’ he says. ‘I only want you to have a special evening.’ Maria looks at him for a moment. Then she starts to laugh. ‘Ivan! Only you can take me to the theatre in November with tickets for April!’ ‘What should we do now?’ he asks. ‘The children are at the neighbour’s and I’m wearing my nicest dress. This evening is ours!’

paragraphs.bg: Иван ѝ дава шала си и те вървят бавно по стария мост над реката. Небето е чисто и пълно със звезди. Те говорят за сватбата си, за децата, за Пловдив. Рядко имат време за това. Мария държи ръката му и вече не усеща студа.
paragraphs.nl: Ivan geeft haar zijn sjaal en ze lopen langzaam over de oude brug over de rivier. De lucht is helder en vol sterren. Ze praten over hun bruiloft, over de kinderen, over Plovdiv. Ze hebben daar zelden tijd voor. Maria houdt zijn hand vast en voelt de kou niet meer.
paragraphs.en: Ivan gives her his scarf and they walk slowly across the old bridge over the river. The sky is clear and full of stars. They talk about their wedding, about the children, about Plovdiv. They rarely have time for this. Maria holds his hand and no longer feels the cold.

paragraphs.bg: След моста има малък бар. Там е топло. Всички са с дънки и пуловери и гледат дългата рокля и костюма. Келнерът им носи чай с мед и лимон. „Колко сте красиви!“, казва той. „От театър ли идвате?“ Иван взема билетите от джоба си и му ги показва. „Не“, казва Мария и се смее. „Отиваме на театър. През април.“
paragraphs.nl: Na de brug is er een kleine bar. Daar is het warm. Iedereen draagt een spijkerbroek en een trui en kijkt naar de lange jurk en het pak. De ober brengt hun thee met honing en citroen. ‘Wat bent u mooi!’ zegt hij. ‘Komt u van het theater?’ Ivan haalt de kaartjes uit zijn zak en laat ze aan hem zien. ‘Nee,’ zegt Maria, en ze lacht. ‘We gaan naar het theater. In april.’
paragraphs.en: After the bridge there is a small bar. It is warm there. Everyone is in jeans and sweaters, and they look at the long dress and the suit. The waiter brings them tea with honey and lemon. ‘How beautiful you are!’ he says. ‘Are you coming from the theatre?’ Ivan takes the tickets out of his pocket and shows them to him. ‘No,’ says Maria, and she laughs. ‘We’re going to the theatre. In April.’
